title: Korea in December: What to Wear and Do
summary: Planning a Korea trip in December? Learn what to pack, how Seoul, Busan, and Jeju differ, and what to enjoy on cold days.

slides.title: Wind Makes Seoul Feel Colder
slides.voice: Seoul’s December wind makes the cold feel worse.
slides.photo_query: Seoul winter street pedestrians padded coats

slides.title: Layers Work Indoors
slides.sub: Bring warm layers you can remove
slides.voice: Pack a padded coat, hat, gloves, and scarf. Use thin layers indoors.

slides.title: Busan Is Milder
slides.sub: Jeju can feel cold in sea winds
slides.voice: Busan is milder; Jeju’s sea winds still feel cold.

slides.title: See Seoul’s Lanterns
slides.voice: See lanterns after dark on a weekday. Check festival dates before you go.

slides.title: Warm Up With Snacks
slides.sub: Try hotteok or fish cakes in broth
slides.voice: Warm up with hotteok or fish cakes in hot broth.

slides.title: New Korea tips
slides.voice: Subscribe for more Korea tips every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
